stories.title: Nextdc CEO to forgo bonus after Australia data centre delay
stories.summary: (Oct 26): Nextdc Ltd’s chief executive officer will give up his short-term and long-term bonuses for the 2027 financial year after the Australia data centre developer warned delayed power supply at one of its major projects in Melbourne would hit profits.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
“The board and management are focused on two priorities: working with our customer and the electricity distributor to minimise the impact of the M3 power delay, as well as earning back the confidence of our investors and other stakeholders,” chairman Douglas Flynn said in a statement ahead of the company’s annual general meeting next month.

Flynn and the company’s non-executive directors agreed to a 10% reduction in their fees, the statement said, adding that the board had also withdrawn a resolution to seek shareholder approval to increase the maximum annual remuneration of non-executive directors to A$2.5 million, from A$2.2 million

CEO Craig Scroggie will not receive any cash or other award in place of his relinquished incentives.

Last week’s news of the delay at the company’s M3 data centre in the Western suburbs of Melbourne prompted the biggest drop in its share price since the company listed in 2010.

Flynn reaffirmed his intention to retire from the board once a new chairman is in place, after a short handover period.

Global search and board advisory firm Spencer Stuart has been hired to find an independent non-executive director and a new chair, according to the statement. The new board members will ideally have data centre, energy or infrastructure development and capital management experience, Nextdc said.

stories.title: SoftBank plans US$50 billion data center investment in Malaysia: Report
stories.summary: SoftBank Group plans to invest US$ 50 billion in Malaysia targetting artificial intelligence and data centers, Bloomberg reports quoting Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said last Saturday he had a video conference with Masayoshi Son, Founder, Chairman and CEO of SoftBank on Tuesday, where the latter had indicated that he was eyeing certain regions […]
stories.content:
SoftBank Group plans to invest US$ 50 billion in Malaysia targetting artificial intelligence and data centers, Bloomberg reports quoting Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said last Saturday he had a video conference with Masayoshi Son, Founder, Chairman and CEO of SoftBank on Tuesday, where the latter had indicated that he was eyeing certain regions in Malaysia including Kuching, Sarawak for digital projects including data centers.

“He said he had chosen Sarawak – Kuching – and peninsular Malaysia to expand investment in what would be among the largest investments in the region, worth US$50 billion,” Anwar said in a speech in Melaka.

Malaysia continues to attract investments – from 2021 till 1H 2026, the country has recorded RM 385.7 billion (US$94 billion) of data center-related investment, according to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA).

The tech investor already has a lot on its plate – the US$ 500 billion Stargate project in the US, a US$ 84 billion project in France, and ongoing data center projects in Hokkaido and Osaka, Japan.

Softbank had earlier this month signed framework agreements with partners including Grab and Sarawak’s government agencies to explore AI infrastructure and ecosystem development in Sarawak.

SoftBank’s representatives did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

stories.title: India's AI builders face GPU, memory, power bottlenecks
stories.summary: Indian AI builders are struggling to secure graphics processing units (GPUs), high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and data center power. Deliveries for GPUs can take three to four months, impacting engineering timelines.
stories.content:
Indian artificial intelligence (AI) builders face significant bottlenecks in securing graphics processing units (GPUs), memory, and data center power and space, according to investors and founders. Deliveries for specialised chips used to train and run AI models can extend to three or four months.The challenge for AI compute in India has shifted from affordability to access, with demand outstripping supply. Early-stage startups often receive Cloud credits, making compute affordability less of an issue in the first year, said Rahul Agarwalla, managing partner at SenseAI Ventures.Companies like Juspay, a Bengaluru-based financial technology firm, face the same procurement queues for GPUs despite being able to front-load investments. Sheetal Lalwani, Cofounder and Chief Operating Officer at Juspay, stated during a media briefing that the company is bottlenecked by the difficulty in getting GPUs allocated, with commitments taking three to six months.Ashish Taneja, founding partner and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of growX ventures, noted that a three to four-month delay for a GPU card can cause an entire engineering team to lose a quarter. This impact on development time is often more detrimental than using a slightly older generation chip.Beyond GPUs, the bottlenecks extend to high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which feeds data to advanced AI chips. Only three companies—SK hynix, Samsung, and Micron—produce HBM at scale. Micron committed its entire 2026 HBM supply by December 2025, while SK hynix secured demand for all its 2026 memory chips by October 2025.Data center capacity and continuous power supply also pose constraints, as GPUs require facilities with stable power and cooling unlike ordinary servers. Lalwani warned that larger players in India could monopolise data center capacity and power in the future, even if chip procurement improves.The government’s IndiaAI Mission has onboarded over 38,000 GPUs for startups and researchers at subsidised rates. However, some companies, like robotics firm CynLr and defence technology firm Armory, require dedicated or local compute for security or real-time operational reasons, which the public pool does not fully address.Gokul N A, founder of CynLr, explained that compute for robotics must be physically wired next to the robot, forcing live training and local compute. A spokesperson for Armory noted that dedicated rack space as metal-as-a-service would better suit their security and diverse workload needs.

stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates RBI's ₹169-crore data centre in Odisha
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) ₹169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Jatni, Odisha. This facility aims to strengthen digital finance and cybersecurity infrastructure in India.
stories.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) ₹169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, officials said.The RBI facility spans 18.55 acres at Info Valley-II in Jatni. It is designed to host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other flagship initiatives, the government stated.This data centre will contribute to expanding the reach, efficiency, and reliability of digital financial services. It will also form a secure digital foundation for India's technology-driven financial economy.The Cybersecurity Training Institute will enhance capability building in cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research, and sector-wide development.Officials noted the site was chosen for its geographical stability. It is located away from seismically active zones and high-risk international border areas, reducing exposure to natural disasters and geopolitical vulnerabilities.The Jatni data centre is the second of its kind, following one in Navi Mumbai. Both facilities aim to provide a secure, resilient, scalable, and future-ready computing ecosystem for the RBI and the broader financial sector.

stories.title: RBI opens Tier-IV data center in Bhubaneswar
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has inaugurated a new ₹169 crore data center complex in Bhubaneswar. This Tier-IV facility aims to enhance the resilience of the country's financial system and improve the uptime of critical services.
stories.content:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has inaugurated a new ₹169 crore data center complex in Bhubaneswar, according to Governor Sanjay Malhotra. The facility, which received its highest Tier-IV accreditation from the Uptime Institute, will operate independently of third-party cloud service providers.Malhotra stated that the new data center will strengthen the resilience of India's financial system. It will also improve the uptime of critical services, including payment systems and government banking operations.
### Operational Resilience and Cybersecurity

The complex will support the RBI’s payment systems, such as the National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) and Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS), which operate continuously. While the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is managed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), its final settlements occur through the RBI’s data centers.Other vital applications, including the e-Kuber platform used by the Centre, state governments, and banks, will also run on this infrastructure. The facility will host applications related to licenses and approvals sought by central bank-regulated entities.The complex includes four independent data centers. The RBI has applied for a platinum rating from the Indian Green Building Council, acknowledging its energy and water efficiency standards.The project also features a cybersecurity training institute. This institute occupies two-thirds of the land and will train RBI personnel, bank employees, and other financial sector staff. Its curriculum covers emerging technologies and cybersecurity, including artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, quantum technology, and blockchain. Malhotra noted that the institute will also conduct research to enhance the security and efficiency of financial systems, especially with the rise of AI.
### Strategic Location Choice

Bhubaneswar was selected for its geographical separation from the RBI’s three existing data centers in Maharashtra, Malhotra explained. This location provides an additional layer of resilience, as it is situated in a different seismic zone. The availability of local talent also influenced the choice of location.

stories.title: KT Cloud begins 50MW Ansan AI data center construction
stories.summary: KT Cloud has started construction on a 50MW AI data center in Ansan, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea, targeting completion in 2029. The facility is designed for high-density AI servers, including features like liquid cooling and reinforced floors for GPUs.
stories.content:
KT Cloud has commenced construction on a 50MW AI data center in Ansan, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea, with completion targeted for 2029. The company announced the Ansan AI Data Center project on October 22, according to Baxtel.CJ Logistics' construction division secured the contract to build the data center. The facility is located within the Banwol National Industrial Complex in Ansan and will encompass approximately 36,878 square metres of gross floor area across two basement levels and nine above-ground floors, The Elec reported.The data center is designed to take in 50MW of power, with 32MW allocated for IT load to actual equipment. Each server room will support liquid cooling, and the building's structure and server room floors are reinforced for high-performance accelerators such as Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs.A free-cooling system will integrate cooling coils on the building's upper exterior walls, connecting them to closed-circuit cooling towers. This system aims to reduce chiller and cooling tower fan power during cooler months.Kim Bong-kyun, CEO of KT Cloud, stated the Ansan AI Data Center incorporates next-generation design technology and power and cooling infrastructure optimised for high-density AI servers, Chosun Biz reported. He added that the company will leverage its experience to deliver stable and efficient AI infrastructure.This Ansan project is part of KT Cloud's broader strategy to deliver 1GW of AI data center capacity by 2031. The company is also developing a 50MW facility in the Cheongna district of Incheon, with construction due to start in late 2026 and completion by early 2030, RCR Wireless News reported. Additionally, work has begun on a 60MW data center in Gunsan with SGC Energy, expected online in early 2028 and scalable to 300MW. KT Cloud previously opened its 26MW Gasan AI Data Center in November 2025.

stories.title: Johor eyes additional 5GW of solar energy by 2031 to meet data centre demand
stories.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI (Oct 25): The Johor government is targeting the generation of about five gigawatts (GW) of solar energy over the next four to five years as a long-term solution to meet the surge in electricity demand driven by the rapid growth of the state’s data centre sector.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
ISKANDAR PUTERI (Oct 25): The Johor government is targeting the generation of about five gigawatts (GW) of solar energy over the next four to five years as a long-term solution to meet the surge in electricity demand driven by the rapid growth of the state’s data centre sector.

State Investment, Trade, Consumer Affairs and Human Resources Committee chairman Lee Ting Han said the strategic move is to ensure the national grid capacity remains robust and capable of balancing industrial and public utility supply requirements following concerns raised in a report by research firm BMI.

BMI, a Fitch Solutions company, estimated that Johor’s data centres would require about 30 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity annually by 2031, accounting for 18% of Peninsular Malaysia’s total electricity supply— up from 6% this year.

On the investment status to date, Lee said the Johor government has approved 65 data centre projects based on land plots.

“Of these, 21 data centres have started operations and they are expected to consume nearly 1.1 GW of electricity, while projects that are still under construction or in the planning stage will require an additional 4GW to 5GW,” he told the media prior to the closing ceremony of the JTDC Mega Job Fair at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre in Iskandar Puteri on Sunday.

Lee said that to ensure the large-scale electricity consumption does not disrupt public utility supply, the state government has established the Johor State Data Centre Development Coordination Committee (JPPPDNJ), which is chaired by Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor, with Lee serving as deputy chairman.

“All proposed data centre developments must first obtain approval from this committee before applying to the local authorities for planning permission.

“The committee also evaluates the power usage effectiveness (PUE) to ensure that electricity is used efficiently and in compliance with the prescribed regulations,” he said.

According to Lee, the state government has taken note of the BMI report, and plans to increase electricity generation capacity are being implemented comprehensively at both state and federal levels.

He said the Energy Commission, under the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation, has called for new tenders to increase power capacity by 8GW across Peninsular Malaysia, with a significant portion of the additional capacity expected to be channelled to Johor.

“At the state level, Johor is intensifying large-scale solar energy projects to diversify electricity supply sources in the Kota Tinggi, Mersing and Segamat areas.

“Overall, these projects are expected to raise Johor’s solar generation capacity by about an additional 5GW by 2030 or 2031 for channeling to data centres and large-scale industries,” he said.

The initiative comprises solar projects totalling 4GW in Kota Tinggi and Mersing, which are expected to start in phases from mid-2029, as well as a 1GW solar project in Segamat.

Lee also welcomed the federal government’s policy allowing operators of large-scale data centres to explore alternative solutions, including off-grid solutions to generate their own electricity, subject to the stipulated regulations.

“These are long-term plans because developing new electricity generation capacity takes a long time. Efforts to increase electricity generation through solar projects, off-grid solutions and new tenders issued by the Energy Commission are being actively pursued by both the Johor government and the federal government.

“We are confident that this careful planning will ensure an adequate electricity supply to support the growth of the data centre industry and other industrial developments in Johor,” he added.

*Read also: Johor data centres could consume over 90% of peninsula's additional power generation by 2031 — BMI*
